ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a two-port resistor ladder network, with a common reference wire below. Along the top, from the left port to the right port, there is successively a 4 Ω series resistor, an internal node A, a 2 Ω series resistor, an internal node B, and then another 2 Ω series resistor to the right port. At node A, there is a 2 Ω resistor connected downward to the common reference line; at node B, there is a 4 Ω resistor connected downward to the common reference line. The left port voltage is labeled E1, and current I1 points into the network; the right port voltage is labeled E2, and current I2 also points into the network. Reasoning: From the h-parameter definition E1 = h11 I1 + h12 E2, therefore h12 is the reverse open-circuit voltage ratio when I1 = 0, that is, h12 = E1/E2. Let input port 1 be open-circuited, so I1 = 0, the current in the left 4 Ω series branch is zero, and its voltage drop is zero; therefore the left port voltage E1 equals the node A voltage VA. Let the right port voltage be E2, and the node A and B voltages be VA and VB respectively. The KCL at node A is: VA/2 + (VA - VB)/2 = 0, giving 2VA - VB = 0, that is, VB = 2VA. The KCL at node B is: VB/4 + (VB - VA)/2 + (VB - E2)/2 = 0. Multiplying both sides by 4 gives VB + 2(VB - VA) + 2(VB - E2) = 0, that is, 5VB - 2VA - 2E2 = 0. Substituting VB = 2VA gives 10VA - 2VA - 2E2 = 0, so 8VA = 2E2, VA/E2 = 1/4. Since E1 = VA, h12 = E1/E2 = 0.25.

The left port voltage is labeled E1, and current I1 points into the network; the right port voltage is labeled E2, and current I2 also points into the network.

Reasoning: From the h-parameter definition E1 = h11 I1 + h12 E2, therefore h12 is the reverse open-circuit voltage ratio when I1 = 0, that is, h12 = E1/E2. Let input port 1 be open-circuited, so I1 = 0, the current in the left 4 Ω series branch is zero, and its voltage drop is zero; therefore the left port voltage E1 equals the node A voltage VA.

Let the right port voltage be E2, and the node A and B voltages be VA and VB respectively. The KCL at node A is: VA/2 + (VA - VB)/2 = 0, giving 2VA - VB = 0, that is, VB = 2VA. The KCL at node B is: VB/4 + (VB - VA)/2 + (VB - E2)/2 = 0. Multiplying both sides by 4 gives VB + 2(VB - VA) + 2(VB - E2) = 0, that is, 5VB - 2VA - 2E2 = 0. Substituting VB = 2VA gives 10VA - 2VA - 2E2 = 0, so 8VA = 2E2, VA/E2 = 1/4. Since E1 = VA, h12 = E1/E2 = 0.25.
